summary: A fully symmetric tree forces any correct algorithm to inspect every mirrored position. The recursive mirror comparison visits each node once and retains one root-to-leaf path per active call chain.

optimality.argument: On a symmetric n-node tree, changing the value or presence of the last unexamined mirrored node would change the answer. A correct algorithm must therefore inspect all n nodes in the worst case, giving Omega(n) time. The current mirror helper compares each node in exactly one mirrored pair and recurses along matching outside and inside directions, so it uses O(n) time and O(h) stack space.

replacement_checks.evidence: A symmetric input cannot be distinguished from a last-position value or structure mismatch without examining every mirrored node.
Each node participates in one mirrored comparison, and the active recursion depth is bounded by tree height h.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover full symmetry and asymmetric null placement; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
